part.title: Booking a holiday sports camp

turns.text: Good morning, Riverside Holiday Sports Camp, Alison Pritchard speaking. How can I help?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Oh, hello. I'm ringing about your summer camp. My daughter's really keen to go, and I wanted to find out a bit more before I book her in.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Of course. How old is she?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: She's ten. I saw a poster that said it's for children from 8 up to 14. Is that right?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Ah, that poster's a bit out of date, I'm afraid. We used to take older children, but now it's 8 to 12, so she'd be absolutely fine.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Great. And what sort of things do they do?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Every morning there's tennis, and then a second sport. Last year that was swimming, but the pool's being repaired this summer, so instead they'll be playing hockey. In the afternoons they can choose between football and athletics.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Oh, she'll love the hockey. She's just started playing it at school.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: And on the last afternoon we finish with a picnic, and families are welcome to come along. We used to put on a sports show, but honestly, the children much prefer the picnic.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: That sounds nice. Right, which weeks are you running?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: We've got three weeks in August. The first one, starting on the 4th, is already full, I'm afraid. But there are still places in the week beginning Monday the 11th, and in the last week, from the 18th.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Hmm, we're away on holiday from the 16th, so it'd have to be the one starting on the 11th.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Fine. So that runs from Monday the 11th to Friday the 15th.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: And how much is it for the week?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: The full price is one hundred and fifty pounds. But if you're a member of the leisure centre, it comes down to one hundred and thirty-five pounds.
turns.text: The full price is £150. But if you're a member of the leisure centre, it comes down to £135.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: We are, yes. We've got a family membership.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: Then it's one hundred and thirty-five pounds. There was an early booking rate of one hundred and twenty pounds, but that finished at the end of May, unfortunately.
turns.text: Then it's £135. There was an early booking rate of £120, but that finished at the end of May, unfortunately.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Never mind. What time does it start each day?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Activities start at nine and finish at half past three. But lots of parents work, so you can drop your child off from 8.15, and there's someone to look after them until things begin.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: That's helpful. I start work at nine myself. And what does she need to bring?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: A packed lunch, because we don't provide food, and trainers, of course. Sun cream's a good idea too. And every child must have a cap, as they're outside most of the day. Some children bring sunglasses, but they often get broken, so we'd rather they didn't.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Right, I'll make sure she's got one. Can I book her in now?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Yes, I'll just fill in the form. What's your daughter's name?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.say: Isla Thackray. That's I, S, L, A, and the surname is T, H, A, C, K, R, A, Y.
turns.text: Isla Thackray. That's I-S-L-A, and the surname is T-H-A-C-K-R-A-Y.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Thank you. And could I check her date of birth? We need it for the insurance.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: It's the 3rd of March, 2015.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Lovely. And what's your home address?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.say: It's 27 Melbury Road. That's M, E, L, B, U, R, Y. It's just behind the station.
turns.text: It's 27 Melbury Road. That's M-E-L-B-U-R-Y. It's just behind the station.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Got it. Does Isla have any medical conditions or allergies we should know about?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: She had asthma when she was younger, but she's grown out of that now. The only thing is nuts. She's allergic to them, so she has to be careful.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Don't worry, we're a nut-free camp anyway, but I'll make a note of it. And a phone number for emergencies?
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.say: Could you put my wife's mobile? I'm a builder, so I don't always hear my phone on site. Hers is oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, five one eight.
turns.text: Could you put my wife's mobile? I'm a builder, so I don't always hear my phone on site. Hers is 07700 900 518.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, five one eight.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: That's right.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Lovely. Last thing. How did you hear about the camp? We like to know which advertising works.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Well, I saw that old poster at the leisure centre, but it was actually the school newsletter that made me ring. There was a piece about you in it last week.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Lovely, I'll put that down. I'll text your wife the booking confirmation and payment details this afternoon.
turns.speaker: coordinator

turns.text: Perfect. Thanks very much for your help.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: You're welcome. Bye.
turns.speaker: coordinator
